entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- Ajay Singh Yadav,G.A.
Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the appellant, learned Additional Government Advocate representing the State as well as learned counsel for the complainant and perused the record.

The instant criminal appeal under Section 14A(1) of SC/ST Act has been filed by the appellant against the order of charge dated 22.10.2024 framed against the appellant by Special Judge, SC/ST Act/ Additional Sessions Judge Ghaziabad in Special Session Trial No. 1269 of 2024 (State Vs.
Rajesh Kumar Rawat) arising out of Case Crime No. 232 of 2024, under Sections 323, 504, 506 IPC and Section 3(2)(Va) of SC/ST Act, Police Station Vijay Nagar, District Ghaziabad.

entities.text: Special Judge, SC/ST Act/ Additional Sessions Judge Ghaziabad
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Police Station Vijay Nagar, District Ghaziabad
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Main substratum argument of learned counsel for the appellant is that one Smt. Sapna Sharma had lodged an F.I.R. dated 03.02.2022, against Vijay Pal Meena registered at Case Crime No. 107 of 2022, under Section 376, 313, 323, 328, 506, 406 I.P.C., Police Station- Vijay Nagar, District- Rajesh Kumar Rawat vs State Of U.P. And Another on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/718824/
1 Ghaziabad, in which the Rajesh Kumar Rawat (appellant herein) was a witness and his statement was recorded during investigation of the said case.

entities.text: Rajesh Kumar Rawat vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since, Vijay Pal Meena is a relative of respondent no.2, therefore, appellant has been falsely implicated in this case.

It is also pointed out that appellant is on bail and pursuant to order dated 22.10.2024, he is facing trial in the present case which is nothing but a malicious prosecution, hence, the order dated 22.10.2024 is liable to be set aside.
On the other hand, learned A.G.A., has vehemently opposed the aforesaid submissions by contending that considering the prosecution case as well as the material collected by the Investigating Officer during investigation, prima facie cognizable offence under Sections under Sections 323, 504, 506 IPC and Section 3(2)(Va) of SC/ST Act is fully made out against the appellant, hence, there is no illegality in the order dated 22.10.2024.

Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and upon perusal of the record, I find that it is well settled that the defence of the accused-appellant cannot be considered at the stage of framing of charge.

Since the allegations made by the prosecution and the defence of the accused-appellant is still open to be urged before the trial court, therefore, this court is not recording any finding on the same.
However, this court is of the view that, in light of Section 216 Cr.P.C., the charge may be altered at any stage of the trial, based on the evidence brought on record by the parties concerned.
In this view of the matter, I do not find any good ground to interfere with the order dated 22.10.2024 passed by the Special Judge, SC/ST Act/ Additional Sessions Judge Ghaziabad.

entities.text: SC/ST Act/ Additional Sessions Judge Ghaziabad
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Accordingly, instant criminal appeal lacks merit and, is hereby dismissed.
